entities.summary: Ulaia binte Almadi was an Abbasid princess, noted for her legacy as a poet and musician. Born into the Al-Mahdi dynasty, she was a member of the Umayyad and Abbasid caliphate families. Her poetry and music were renowned throughout the Abbasid Empire, particularly in the cities of Baghdad and Damascus. Ulaia binte Almadi's work was often praised for its beauty, wit, and intellectual depth. She was a favorite among the Abbasid caliphs, including Harun al-Rashid, who patronized her artistic endeavors. Ulaia binte Almadi's legacy continued to inspire generations of poets and musicians in the Middle East and North Africa. Despite her passing in 825 CE, her work remains an important part of Islamic cultural heritage. In the words of her contemporary poet, 'Ulaia binte Almadi's poetry is like a rose in bloom, its beauty and fragrance never fading with time.'
